# **HYDROCOPPER**<sup>**®**</sup> **– MOVING UP IN THE COPPER PRODUCTION CHAIN** 

Liisa Haavanlammi<sup>1</sup> , Janne Karonen<sup>2</sup> , Claudio Rodrнguez<sup>3</sup> 

Outokumpu Technology Oy Riihitontuntie 7C, P.O. Box 86, FIN- 02201 Espoo, Finland Tel: +358 94212163, Fax: +358 9 4213973 

Outokumpu Technology Chile Avda. Vitacura 2939, Piso 9, Las Condes, Chile Tel: +56023362083, Fax: +56023362051 

1Technology Sales Manager – HydroCopper®, liisa.haavanlammi@outokumpu.com 2Development Manager - Copper Hydrometallurgy, janne.karonen@outokumpu.com 3Sales & Process Engineer – Hydrometallurgy, claudio.rodrнguez@outokumpu.com 

# **<u>ABSTRACT</u>** 

HydroCopper<sup>®</sup> is a chloride based leaching process developed by Outokumpu Technology in Finland. The process is capable of leaching all kinds of copper sulfide concentrates in atmospheric pressure. The main leaching agent is copper (II) ion, aided by the strong, nearly saturated sodium chloride solution and oxygen as oxidant. Copper is precipitated from the purified pregnant leach solution as copper (I) oxide, which is filtered and reduced by hydrogen gas to metallic copper powder. The powder is melted and cast into copper product. The product of the process is copper metal in a semiproduct form, which means one step further from the copper cathode production. The product can be wire rod at any diameter, billet, slab or strip, depending on the producer’s choice. The HydroCopper<sup>®</sup> process gives an alternative to the concentrate producer to move up in the production chain. The HydroCopper<sup>®</sup> plant can be situated either at the mine site, or it can function as a stand-alone plant with feed material from various sources. 

# **<u>RESUMEN</u>** 

HydroCopper<sup>®</sup> es un proceso basado en la lixiviaciуn en medio clorhнdrico, desarrollado por Outokumpu Technology en Finlandia. El proceso es capaz de lixiviar todos los tipos de concentrados de sulfuros de cobre a presiуn atmosfйrica. El principal agente de lixiviaciуn es el ion del cobre (II), ayudado por la fuerza de la soluciуn de cloruro de sodio y el oxнgeno como oxidante. El cobre es precipitado, desde la soluciуn rica de lixiviaciуn purificada como уxido de cobre (I), este es filtrado y reducido por el gas de hidrуgeno a polvo de cobre metбlico. El polvo se funde y se moldea como producto de cobre. El producto del proceso es metal de cobre en una forma de semi-producto, que significa un paso mбs lejos de la producciуn de cobre catуdico. El producto puede ser barra de alambre de cualquier diбmetro, lamina, bloque o tira, dependiendo de la opciуn del productor. El proceso de HydroCopper<sup>®</sup> da una alternativa al productor del concentrado a elevar su cadena de producciуn. La planta de HydroCopper<sup>®</sup> se puede ubicar en el mismo sitio de la mina, o puede funcionar como una planta independiente con el material de la alimentaciуn de varias fuentes. 

# **1. INTRODUCTION** 

Since the 1970’s, there have

been many new hydrometallurgical processes developed for the treatment of copper sulphide ores and concentrates. Almost all of these have included solvent extraction (SX) and/or electrowinning (EW) in the process route to produce a cathode or powder product. Outokumpu Technology has developed a unique process called HydroCopper<sup>®</sup> which produces a high purity and high value oxygen free copper product that may be sold directly to manufacturers. 

This process allows mining companies to take control of the complete mine to metal process route, bypass the custom smelters and rod companies and realize the benefits of the downstream added value process steps. When the HydroCopper<sup>®</sup> process is combined with the concentrator at the mine site, the process may be optimized to maximize copper recoveries and economize the performance of the whole process chain from mine to metal. 



**Figure 1. HydroCopper**<sup>**®**</sup> **- An Alternative Route for Processing Copper Metal** 

# **2. OUTOKUMPU HYDROCOPPER**<sup>**®**</sup> **PROCESS DESCRIPTION** 



**Figure 2. HydroCopper**<sup>**®**</sup> **process** 

The HydroCopper<sup>®</sup> process (Figure 2) consists of three steps to produce copper powder; leaching of copper concentrate, solution purification, precipitation of copper (I) oxide and reduction to copper powder. 

The lixiviant (sodium chloride) is regenerated in a chlor-alkali electrolyser cell and oxygen free high purity copper wire rod or any other cast copper product is produced via an induction furnace and a copper upcasting machine (Haavanlammi, Hyvдrinen, Yllц, 2005). 

# <u>Leaching</u> 

Leaching takes place in agitated reactors at atmospheric pressure and temperature of 85 –100 deg C. Three countercurrent stages are required to leach chalcopyrite concentrate, with a thickener after each stage for liquid/solid separation.  Total retention time in copper leaching varies between 15 – 25 

hours. The most important factor in leaching is the mineralogy of the raw material used. Not only can the copper minerals’ leaching rates differ; gangue materials and iron mineralogy will also have an influence on leaching. 

Concentrate, a strong sodium chloride solution and air or oxygen are used in all the leaching stages to generate a strongly oxidizing environment for the copper and gold in concentrate to leach as effectively as possible. The main leaching agent is Cu<sup>2+</sup> , which leaches copper out of the concentrate. The Cu<sup>+</sup> formed is oxidized back to Cu<sup>2+</sup> with chlorine gas produced in the chlor-alkali cell. 

In the first stage fresh concentrate is mixed with the leaching solution from the second stage of leaching. In this stage generally 15 – 30% of the copper will be leached. In the second stage the leaching pH is controlled to a level of 2.0 – 2.4 by air or oxygen to leach the majority of the copper. The third leaching stage is also oxidative and will leach the remaining 2 – 5% of the copper in c

oncentrate. Copper yield in leaching has been at least 98% for every concentrate tested. 

If gold is present in the concentrate, it starts to leach after most of the copper in concentrate has been leached. Gold leaches, when the redox-potential of the leaching solution is raised to a 650 mV (Ag/AgCl) level. The leaching rate and efficiency depend greatly on the mineralogy of the concentrate. 

The final leach residue is filtered out of the underflow from the thickener after the third leaching stage. The leach residue consists primarily of elemental sulfur and hematite. 

# <u>Filtering of the products and residues</u> 









































**Figure 3. The demo plant leaching residue filter** 

Vacuum belt filters were used for leaching residue (Figure 3) and copper (I) oxide powder filtering. The filterabilities of the solids were very good, better than expected after the laboratory experiments. The belt filter application was selected for the product and residue filtering, because in most cases they both need very intensive, multi-stage washing. In both of the solids the chloride content has to be washed down in order to avoid NaCl losses. 

# <u>Solution Purification</u> 

Solution purification is carried out in four stages; cupric precipitation, silver removal, metal precipitation and ion exchange. 

# Cupric Precipitation 

In the first stage of solution purification, the pregnant leach solution is treated with limestone to remove sulfate - formed from sulfur in leaching - as gypsum, and caustic soda at pH 4 to precipitate the remaining copper (II) as cupric hydroxychloride called atacamite. The precipitate is circulated back to leaching, where gypsum reports to the leaching residue. Atacamite is re-leached and thus copper losses to the residue are avoided. 

# Silver Removal 

In the second stage of solution purification, metallic copper powder and some mercury solution is added to fluid bed type reactors. The copper ensures that any remaining copper (II) ions are reduced to copper (I) and silver cements onto the copper forming a silver-mercury amalgam. When this reaction is complete, the solution (containing less than 1 mg/L silver and mercury below detectable limits) is taken to the next solution purification stage. 

The silver-mercury amalgam is treated with an oxidative leaching process. Silver is recovered as silver chloride and the mercury chloride solution is circulated back to the silver removal stage. The silver chloride can be further purified to metallic silver, if desired. 

# Metal Precipitation 

In the third stage of solution purification, sodium carbonate is added and most of the metals (Zn, Pb Ni etc.,) are precipitated as carbonates at pH 6 – 6.5. The main controlling factor in this stage of the process is pH. By careful control pH can be kept low enough not to precipitate any copper from the leaching solution. 

# Ion Exchange 

In order to achieve a high purity copper product, the final solution puri

fication must be by ion exchange. This takes out the remaining metallic impurities in addition to calcium and magnesium. 

The resin used is a selective chelating type cation exchange resin. The weak elution acids used in the ion exchange are circulated either back to the process 

or the acid fractions can be separated to allow an impurity bleed from the process. 

# <u>Precipitation of Cuprous Oxide</u> 

The third step of the process is the precipitation of copper (I) oxide. Sodium hydroxide liquor from the chlor-alkali electrolytic cell precipitates the copper (I) oxide as powder at pH 9 - 10. The slurry is washed and filtered on a vacuum belt filter (Figure 4) while the filtrate, sodium chloride solution, is sent to the chlor-alkali cell. 



**Figure 4. Cuprous oxide powder on the belt filter** 

# <u>Reduction to Copper Powder</u> 

Copper (I) oxide from the precipitation step is then fed to a belt furnace with temperatures in the range of 650 – 850 deg C and with hydrogen-nitrogen flow. The hydrogen gas used in the reduction furnaces is produced in the chlor-alkali cell. In this stage the oxygen content is reduced to a level of 200 – 300 ppm and the copper powder discharged, having been slightly sintered. 

# <u>Casting a Copper Product</u> 

The reduced copper plates from the belt furnace can be converted to a high purity oxygen free copper product such as slabs, strips, billet or rod via an induction furnace. The furnace has a graphite layer on top to remove the remaining oxygen (Figure 5). 



**Figure 5. Graphite layer on top of the copper melt in the induction furnace** 

# <u>Regeneration of Chemicals – Chlor-alkali Technology</u> 

A key feature of the HydroCopper<sup>®</sup> process is the use of chlor-alkali electrolysis for the regeneration of chemicals. The sodium chloride filtrate generated at the precipitation of cuprous oxide is fed to the chlor-alkali electrolysis cell, where the salt and water are decomposed by electricity to sodium hydroxide, chlorine and hydrogen. 

The sodium hydroxide is used to the precipitation of copper (I) oxide and atacamite, the chlorine gas is used in the leaching and the hydrogen gas is used in the reduction to copper powder. No intermediate storage for gaseous components is needed within the plant, the gases are produced for direct usage within the HydroCopper<sup>®</sup> process. 

Chlor-alkali technology is well proven and widely used technology to produce chemicals and is used in the forest industry as well chemical industries such as plastics. The chloralkali plant within the HydroCopper<sup>®</sup> plant can be designed to meet the requirements of the HydroCopper<sup>®</sup> process or, if there is a market for the products of the cell, hydrochloric acid or caustic soda, they can be produced in to the markets as well. 

A major concern for the operation was the quality of the sodium chloride at the inlet to the chlor-alkali cell, because the cell manufacturers set strict quality requireme

nts for the feed. The advantage of the HydroCopper® process is that the brine concentration is naturally set at the required concentration and the solution purification and copper (I) oxide precipitation are designed to remove the impurities down to trace levels in the brine feed. In addition the cell is safeguarded with its own ion exchange to ensure that the last traces of calcium and magnesium and copper are removed. After the test campaigns no signs of copper contamination were evident in the cell. # **3. EFFECTIVE LOGISTICS – HYDROCOPPER AT MINESITE** A HydroCopper® plant is at its most effective, when built in connection with a concentrator. The whole production chain can be optimised according to the requirements of the ore body. Total copper recovery from mine to metal can be optimised within the whole production chain. The HydroCopper® process is a very versatile process, which can easily cope with the changes in the concentrate feed. The copper content in the concentrate can be as low as, for example 12%, which means that the process can be adapted to the rougher concentrates. This in most cases increases the copper recovery at the concentrator by at least 10% (Figure 6). ®
**Figure 6. HydroCopper production chain** If the copper is produced at the mine site, it reduces significantly the logistics both volume and cost-wise. Transporting concentrate is easier than transporting copper metal, but the volumes transported out of the plant area are 75% lower, if the concentrate copper content is 25%. The leaching residue from the plant can be stored within the concentrator tailings. Working capital requirements are substantially reduced since the concentrate is processed to copper product within days and shipped directly to customers or exchange markets. This allows realization of revenues months faster than when selling concentrate. **Figure 7. Copper Wire Rod Ready to Leave the Production Plant** Most of the chemicals used in the HydroCopper® process are produced and regenerated within the process. Calcium is the only component that has to be purchased outside. The actual input requirements depend on the concentrate composition and are confirmed after tests have been carried out. The outside inputs therefore may be considered broadly as follows: - power (Electricity) for agitators, pumps, chlor-alkali electrolyser and miscellaneous items; - calcium compound for solution purification; - steam for clean condensate supply and for evaporation of excess water; # **4. FROM CONCENTRATE MARKETS TO COPPER BUSINESS** For a copper concentrate producer the HydroCopper® process gives an opportunity to move up in the copper production chain. The product of the HydroCopper® process is one step further from a basic copper cathode, which gives the producer a chance to move to the copper product

ion business. If the product is chosen to be 8 mm wire rod, the markets are strong and give a lot of possibilities around the world (Table 1). Consumption of copper wire rod is increasing and the main applications are in the telecommunications industry and power cables (Figure 8), according to CRU. **Figure 8. Copper Wire Rod End-Use Segments** When HydroCopper® business is compared to concentrate sales, there are specific areas, where the HydroCopper® option can lead to significant savings. The product being a copper wire rod, there are no TC/RC charges. The product also has a valueadded premium in sales compared to selling copper cathode. For bigger deposits the opportunities are wider, and the ore can be divided to two; the first being the conventional copper concentrate market and the second one the HydroCopper® process. The same concentrator facility can be used to produce concentrate for both options. There might be parts of the ore body, where for example arsenic, antimony or bismuth is present at larger quantities. The HydroCopper® plant could be designed to treat the dirty fraction of the concentrate whereas the cleaner fractions can be sold to the concentrate markets. # **5. CONCLUSIONS** The Outokumpu HydroCopper® process is a proven way to begin production of high quality copper. When attached to a concentrator at the mine site, the process is an economical way to produce a premium copper product directly saleable to the copper market and to economize the whole production chain from mine to copper metal. There are multiple ways to integrate the HydroCopper® facility to the concentrator. The HydroCopper process can be built to treat a variety of concentrates, and the plant is ® economical in the smaller capacities, starting from 20’000 tons of copper metal per annum. The economics of an integrated mine

to metal concept can be evaluated case by case using Outokumpu Technology’s testing facilities in Pori, Finland and also the engineering experience of Outokumpu Technology. 

Copper miners and producers now have an opportunity to enter the copper product business using the cost efficient Outokumpu HydroCopper<sup>®</sup> process.
